acts.name: Where it actually began
acts.desc: Three churches founded between 1896 and 1919 — none of them a street camp

acts.name: The movement splits
acts.desc: A farming village in Israel and a Harlem camp go in opposite directions

acts.name: The clips and the label
acts.desc: Street confrontations go viral, a hate-group listing lands, and the movement argues with itself

turningPoints.1896: A formerly enslaved Union veteran founded the first documented body; it still exists today
turningPoints.1966–69: A whole community moved to Israel and built a peaceable village that still stands
turningPoints.1969–80s: One Harlem address produced the chart, the Edomite doctrine, and every confrontational camp since
turningPoints.2000: A dated prophecy failed publicly, and the movement's own record shows the rebrand that followed
turningPoints.2016: A hate-group listing of specific camps fixed how outsiders now see the whole movement
